subject: research/qual-hypothesis
professional: a statistician / NLP researcher reviewing for a workshop on hypothesis generation from text. They would check first that the selection-then-validate pipeline (sample splitting, two-proportion z, Benjamini-Hochberg) is implemented right, that the 'inflation' metric actually estimates shrinkage, that the null calibration has the stated error rate, and whether the work is positioned against the winner's-curse literature (Zhong & Prentice 2008) and LLM hypothesis proposers (Zhong et al. 2022, D3)

evidence.correctness: Reran experiments/run.py in a scratch copy (the repo tree untouched): results.txt byte-identical to the committed file (46 s, GoEmotions goemotions_1.csv sha256 cac04903...af3, 14,174,600 bytes, downloaded from the authors' public bucket). Then my own pipeline (scratchpad indep.py: own CSV loader, numpy, statsmodels proportions_ztest for the pooled z and multipletests fdr_bh for BH): N 5,313, share 0.2469; on the E3 split (same permutation, random.Random(20261020+1)) all 20 words, discovery effects, held-out effects, p values and replicate flags equal results.txt E3 (11 replicate). BH vs the author's benjamini_hochberg on 20,000 random p-vectors (m 1-29, with ties): 0 disagreements. Independent Monte Carlo with my own seeds (200 splits per row) lands within Monte Carlo error: disc/held |effect| 0.0950/0.0124 (author 0.0948/0.0125) at n=100, 0.0212/0.0141 at 2,000 (0.0211/0.0141); replicated 0.62, 3.37, 10.19, 14.65 (author 0.80, 3.55, 10.31, 14.65); shuffled-label splits with any replicate 3.0/2.5/3.5/5.0% (author 2.5/3.0/2.5/5.5%), Wilson intervals all cover 5%. The arithmetic is right. What keeps it from 4: the 'held-out effect' is the mean of |d| on held-out data, which carries a noise floor (shuffled labels give 0.009 where the truth is 0); sign-aligned, the held-out effect at n=100 is 0.0028, so the inflation is about 34x, not the 7.6x reported. 3.

But the milestone the project exists for (PROJECTS.md:1398, marked 'done 2026-10-20') is 'LLM-proposed, human-readable hypotheses ... with a check for hypotheses that merely restate the label': no LLM proposer exists (a word counter stands in, disclosed), hypotheses are single tokens, and the restatement check is a fixed word list the README itself calls crude and incomplete. Running the project alone fails: it imports ../qual-real and ../qual-correction via sys.path. 2.

Seeded 7 mutations in qualhyp.py with platform/ci/quality_mutate.py: caught 2 (BH cut off by one, p value erfc(|z|/2)); survived 5: BH replaced by Bonferroni (alpha*rank/m -> alpha/m; the only BH test vector gives the same set under both), the same-sign requirement for replication removed, min_count filter disabled, pooled proportion (a+b) -> (a+1), proposer ranking by |d| instead of |z|. The core of the method (BH step-up, sign check, ranking, variance) is essentially untested. 1.
evidence.craft: Read qualhyp.py (90 lines), test_qualhyp.py, experiments/run.py, figure.py, and the reused qual-real/qualreal.py loader and run.py fetch. Small, stdlib, readable, seeded and deterministic. Defects: the reused tokenizer [a-z']+ splits on the curly apostrophe U+2019 used in 673 of 5,313 comments, so 'I’m' becomes 'i' + 'm' (106 of 113 comments with token 'm'), and 'm', 't', 'don' enter the hypothesis family; 'm' is reported as a confirmed hypothesis in E3. The download has no checksum pin. Cross-project sys.path imports (qualhyp.py:13, run.py:15) chain three research dirs. restates_label rebuilds set(r.NEGATIVE) per call (trivial). 3.
evidence.claims: Backed: every number in the README tables equals results.txt and reproduces; the 'not an LLM' limit is up front; data is downloaded, not committed, and the Apache 2.0 licence matches the dataset card (huggingface go_emotions README: 'Apache License 2.0'); citations-from-memory are disclosed; the page carries the AI-assistance disclaimer. Not backed: (1) README:52 says the shuffled-label discovery effect of 0.09 'is really 0.01'; it is really 0, the 0.009 is the |d| noise floor (sign-aligned held-out mean -0.0002); (2) the headline '7.6 times too large' and '1.5 times' are ratios to a noise-inflated held-out |d|, so they understate the inflation at small n (sign-aligned 34x at n=100, 1.53x at 2,000); (3) the headline '36-59% of confirmed hypotheses are label vocabulary' omits the 6.9% at n=100 in its own table; (4) PROJECTS.md:1398 marks the LLM-proposer milestone done. 2.
evidence.fitness: A researcher wanting to build an LLM hypothesis proposer gets a reusable held-out validation harness (split, two-proportion z, BH, null control) on a real corpus, which is useful. But the finding, that effects selected as the most extreme of thousands shrink on fresh data and that sample splitting plus BH controls error under the null, is the textbook winner's curse / selective inference result (Zhong & Prentice 2008, Biostatistics; Cox 1975 sample splitting; Wasserman & Roeder 2009), and the nearest NLP prior work is not cited: Zhong, Snell, Klein & Steinhardt 2022 'Describing differences between text distributions with natural language' (D3) proposes hypotheses with an LLM and validates them on held-out samples, the exact pipeline here with a real proposer; Zhong et al. 2023 (D5, goal-driven discovery); Monroe, Colaresi & Quinn 2008 'Fightin' words', the standard word-level two-corpus comparison that the counting proposer re-derives; Zhou et al. 2024 HypoGeniC. Only Ludwig & Mullainathan 2024 is cited. The restatement result (label words confirm) is expected when the hypothesis space is the label's vocabulary. Not new; sound in its arithmetic, not in its shrinkage metric. 2.
evidence.domain: Against selective-inference practice: sample splitting with BH on the held-out family is the right design, the pooled two-proportion z is standard, and the global-null calibration is correct (FWER = FDR under the complete null; observed 2.5-5.5%). Departures: shrinkage should be measured by the sign-aligned held-out estimate (or a bias-corrected / conditional estimator, as in the winner's-curse literature), not mean |d|; FDR is checked only under the complete null, never in the mixed real-label setting (e.g. by planting known effects), which is where BH's guarantee matters; no Monte Carlo uncertainty is reported for any table entry; the restatement flag only covers negative-emotion words, so the confirmed words at n=100 ('people', 'are', 'love', 'good', 'lol' in my 200 splits) are mostly the label's positive antonyms and go uncounted. A reviewer would ask for these before accepting. 2.

defects.what: The held-out 'effect' is mean |d| over the 20 hypotheses, which includes a sampling-noise floor (0.009 with shuffled labels where the truth is 0). The headline inflation '7.6 times' at n=100 is therefore understated (sign-aligned held-out effect 0.0028, ratio about 34x), and README:52 misreads the null case as 'really 0.01'

Nearest prior work not cited and novelty not positioned: Zhong et al. 2022 D3 (LLM proposer + held-out validation of hypotheses about two text distributions), winner's curse / sample splitting (Zhong & Prentice 2008; Cox 1975; Wasserman & Roeder 2009), Monroe et al. 2008 Fightin' words for the counting proposer

Tests miss the method's core: replacing BH with Bonferroni, removing the same-sign requirement, disabling min_count, corrupting the pooled variance, or ranking by |d| all leave the 7 tests green (2 of 7 mutants caught)

Milestone 6 marked done though its stated content (LLM-proposed hypotheses, a check for label restatement) is not built: the proposer is a word counter and the restatement check is a fixed negative-word list that cannot see positive antonyms ('love', 'good' dominate confirmations at n=100)
Tokenizer [a-z']+ splits on the curly apostrophe (673 of 5,313 comments), so 'I’m', 'don’t' yield hypotheses 'm', 't', 'don'; 'm' is reported as a confirmed hypothesis without noting it is 'I'm'
Headline '36-59% of confirmed hypotheses are label vocabulary' omits the 6.9% at 100 discovery comments shown in its own table
FDR control is shown only under the complete null (where FDR = FWER); no planted-effect mixture checks BH in the real-label regime, and no Monte Carlo uncertainty is reported for any table entry
GoEmotions download is not checksum-pinned (observed sha256 cac049036bad5d68d1081f72b65f2cc51e4df82af05e3e22cfa747051cac1af3); a changed bucket file would change results silently

verdict: The arithmetic is right and reproducible: run.py regenerates results.txt byte for byte, my own statsmodels-based pipeline reproduces every row of the E3 split exactly, BH agrees with statsmodels on 20,000 random vectors, and an independent Monte Carlo lands within error of every E1/E2 entry, with the shuffled-label any-discovery rate at 2.5-5% as BH promises. It does not meet the bar (verification 1, claims 2, median 2). The inflation metric divides by mean |held-out d|, a noise floor, so the headline '7.6 times' understates the winner's curse (about 34x sign-aligned at n=100) and the README misreads the null as 'really 0.01'; 5 of 7 seeded bugs in the BH step, sign check, ranking and variance survive the tests; the milestone (LLM proposer, restatement check) is marked done but not built; and the result is the textbook winner's curse / sample-splitting finding, without citing the closest NLP prior work (Zhong et al. 2022, D3).
